messages:
nina: Heads-up — ran a perf sweep of the 13B onboarding workload across providers. On GCP A100 (CUDA 11.8, driver 525) we're seeing ~30-40% higher p99 latency vs AWS A100 (CUDA 11.7, driver 520) with identical container and model config. Anyone else seen a stack-level delta like this? :thinking:

sam: Can you paste the bench command and the exact numbers? p50/p95/p99 and throughput would help.

nina: Sure. Quick paste of the run and a small output snippet:
```bash
run_bench --model redwood-13b --batch 1 --seq 2048 --iters 200 --device gpu --quant none
# GCP (a100, cuda11.8, driver525) -> p50 45ms, p95 130ms, p99 240ms, tps 17
# AWS (a100, cuda11.7, driver520) -> p50 32ms, p95 95ms, p99 160ms, tps 23
```
We pinned the same container digest and model weights. No autoscaling differences — single pinned instance.

leo: That magnitude smells like kernel selection differences (cuBLAS/cuDNN/attention kernels). Check the CUDA runtime/cuBLAS versions inside the container (ldd /usr/local/lib/python*/site-packages/torch/lib/libcublas.so?). Also are both machines on the same ECC/clock governor settings?

maria: We saw something similar last quarter — GCP images sometimes ship with a newer driver that flips the GPU clock policy to "adaptive" on idle which can spike p99 for short-lived requests. Try `nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK` and compare clocks under load.

jaspreet: +1 to leo. Also run `nsys profile` for a few iters to see if there are kernel launch stalls or excessive memcpy. Example: `nsys profile -t cuda,osrt -o gcp-a100.nsys ./run_bench ...`

nina: Good calls. I ran a quick nsys capture: shows repeated tiny kernel launches in attention forward on GCP that aren't aggregated (lots of 1-3ms kernels) whereas AWS shows fewer, longer kernels. Could be different flash-attn/cuDNN fallback paths.

sam: Did you try toggling the assembly kernels vs cuBLAS? E.g. env `FORCE_FLASH_ATTENTION=1` or the opposite. Also check `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA` / `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` placement differences.

maria: Also check PCIe vs NVLink topology. On our infra, GCP instances we used had PCIe-only A100s while AWS had NVLink-enabled pods for that SKU — inter-GPU link differences change latency patterns for KV-cache heavy workloads.

leo: For a quick hypothesis test: spin up the same image on a small GCP instance but downgrade the driver to 520 (same as AWS) and re-run. If p99 drops to match, it's driver/kernel. If not, it's likely host firmware/PCIe or microcode. Can we schedule a quick repro job?

nina: I can spin a repro. Action plan: 1) run repro with driver 520 on GCP (nina) 2) run nsys on both machines and upload traces (jaspreet + nina) 3) toggle flash-attn/cublas kernel envs (sam) 4) compare nvidia-smi clock logs under synthetic load (maria). I'll post results here when available.

infra-bot: sched:prov-job-8892 created for `nina` on gcp-a100-520 (ETA 8m). Logs to /jobs/prov-job-8892.

nina: Thanks — will update in ~30m. If anyone has existing traces or a quick script to normalize clock settings across clouds, drop it here. :eyes:
